sections.html:
Bedford County lies in Virginia's Piedmont, reaching toward the Blue Ridge, with the town of Bedford as its seat. It spans 769 square miles and had 79,462 residents in 2020. Lynchburg, an independent city, sits on its edge, and many newer homes here serve people who commute to Lynchburg or Roanoke or who live near Smith Mountain Lake.

Bedford was an independent city from 1968 and went back to town status, rejoining the county on July 1, 2013. If an older deed or letter names the city, ask which office has your parcel on its books. Some unincorporated areas also carry mailing addresses in the town of Bedford or in Lynchburg, so look for the county name on your bill instead of trusting the envelope.

Real estate tax is paid in two parts, the first due June 5 and the second due December 5. A change began in 2026. Before then, one spring bill carried two payment coupons. Now owners receive two separate bills, one in spring and one in fall.

InstallmentDue dateBill
First paymentJune 5Spring bill
Second paymentDecember 5Fall bill
Whole year at onceWith the spring billNo fall bill follows

Paying the full amount in spring saves a second trip. Either way, an owner about to sell should ask the treasurer which bills are paid.

• Online by bank draft or credit card.
  • By mail.
  • In the drop box.
  • In person at the county office, 122 East Main Street, Bedford, VA 24523.

The bill itself shows the tax rate, and the county can be reached at 540-586-7601 with questions about rates, penalty or interest. Call before a deadline passes, not after.

The county is reassessing all real estate, with new values effective January 1, 2027. It hired Wingate Appraisal Service, a firm approved by the Virginia Department of Taxation, to bring assessed values up to current market value, which Virginia law requires localities to do from time to time.

Appraisal staff walk neighborhoods and look at the outside of properties. They may take photos for internal use only, and they leave a flyer when nobody is home. Their vehicles are marked Real Estate Assessment/Wingate Appraisal Service, and staff wear ID badges. Owners get reassessment notices ahead of the January 1, 2027 effective date. Questions go to the Reassessment Office at 540-587-0745.

Appeals go to the local Board of Equalization. Call the Reassessment Office to learn the filing dates and process that apply to your notice.

Under Virginia Code section 58.1-3381 the board has to take up and decide every petition. It can raise, lower or leave a value as is, and an owner must hear about a proposed increase first. Virginia Cooperative Extension puts the board stage at one to three months.

When the board leaves the dispute unsettled, an owner may apply to circuit court under section 58.1-3984. The window is the later of three years after the end of the tax year or one year after the assessment date, among other listed cases. In court the assessor's value starts out presumed right, and the owner must overcome it with a greater weight of evidence.

sections.h2: Should you sell before or after January 2027?
sections.html:
The answer depends on the number in your notice. A higher value means a larger bill after January 1, 2027, and a lower one means less. Compare the notice with what you expect a buyer to pay.

  • Read the notice as soon as it comes and note the appeal window.
  • Ask the Reassessment Office how to request a review if the value looks wrong.
  • Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure for the current year before you close.

A sale before the new values apply lets you settle on the old numbers. A sale after means the buyer carries the new bill from day one, and that can shape what buyers offer.

Tax debt follows the property. Virginia Code section 58.1-3340 gives the locality a lien that comes before other liens until the tax is paid, and proceeds of a sale go first to the taxes. Your share for the current year is prorated by contract.

State law also caps late charges. Section 58.1-3916 limits the penalty to 10 percent of the overdue tax or $10, whichever is greater, with interest of up to 10 percent a year. Ask the treasurer what Bedford actually charges.

Transfer costs on the deed are separate. The grantor tax in section 58.1-802 runs fifty cents for each $500 and falls on the seller unless both sides agree to move it, and the state recordation tax in section 58.1-801 is 25 cents per $100.

sections.h2: Who sells to a cash buyer in Bedford County?
sections.html:
People who inherited a house, rent one that needs work or live out of the area often pick cash. A reassessment, two separate tax bills a year and a house that needs repairs can each push that choice.

We purchase as is. If a Bedford County house is on your mind, phone or text us the address and we will send a written cash offer.

faqs.q: When are Bedford County property taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5. Starting in 2026, owners receive two separate bills, one in the spring and one in the fall.

faqs.q: When does the Bedford County reassessment take effect?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027. Notices go out ahead of that date.

faqs.q: Who is doing the Bedford County reassessment?
faqs.a: Wingate Appraisal Service, hired by the county and approved by the Virginia Department of Taxation. Call 540-587-0745 with questions.

faqs.q: Is the town of Bedford separate from Bedford County?
faqs.a: Bedford was an independent city from 1968 and reverted to a town, then rejoined the county on July 1, 2013. It is the county seat.

faqs.q: How can I pay my Bedford County real estate tax?
faqs.a: Online by bank draft or credit card, by mail, in the drop box or in person at 122 East Main Street, Bedford.
